_why_two_claims: AGREEMENT asks whether the engines compute the same thing; RECOVERY asks whether they compute the right thing. Neither implies the other.

truth.source: the fixture's data-generating process: risks 0.20 treated and 0.30 control

agreement.claim: both engines report the same risks, Newcombe interval, risk ratio and log interval, and NNT with its interval
agreement._note: Observed spread on the committed fixture: 0 at ten significant digits on every key. R writes Newcombe and Katz out over the binom package's Wilson bounds; Python uses statsmodels' confint_proportions_2indep, a separate implementation. harness/categorical_examples.test.py checks both against the formulas and shows the Wald difference interval is a different number.

recovery.claim: the risk difference and log risk ratio are close to the values the fixture was built with

calibration.rule: about 1.3 times the measured 99th percentile miss, rounded up
calibration.limits: At 300 per arm the risk difference's miss (0.087) nearly equalled the effect (0.10) and 23 of 100 intervals crossed zero; the fixture uses 800 per arm. The NNT has no recovery check: it is 1/|RD| and inherits the risk difference's.
